## Problem

`unshortenGeneric` treats the entire HTTP response body as the expanded URL. It checks no status code, parses nothing, and trims nothing. Neither of its two call sites returns a bare URL in the body:

- tinyurl: the endpoint is `http://tinyurl.com/api-create.php?=url=`. `api-create.php` *creates* a short URL, it does not expand one; and the query string is `?=url=` (an empty parameter name), not `?url=`.
- is.gd: `https://is.gd/forward.php?format=json&shorturl=` returns JSON (`{"url":"..."}`), not a bare URL.

The returned garbage then flows into `validateURLAccessibility`, whose `http.Head` fails on a non-URL string, which makes `expandAndCheckURL` return an error, which `processBookmark` converts to `ActionDelete`.</problem>
<parameter name="evidence">main.go:766-783 — no status check, body returned verbatim:

```go
func unshortenGeneric(shortURL, apiURL string) (string, error) {
	resp, err := http.Get(apiURL + shortURL)
	...
	longURL, err := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
	...
	return string(longURL), nil
}
```

main.go:725-734 — the two call sites:

```go
case strings.HasPrefix(cleanedURL, "tinyurl.com/"):
	result, err := unshortenGeneric(shortURL, "http://tinyurl.com/api-create.php?=url=")
case strings.HasPrefix(cleanedURL, "is.gd/"):
	result, err := unshortenGeneric(shortURL, "https://is.gd/forward.php?format=json&shorturl=")
```

main.go:587-595 — the returned value is immediately used as a URL:

```go
expandedURL, err := expandURL(url, verbose)
if err != nil { return "", err }
if err := validateURLAccessibility(expandedURL, "expanded URL"); err != nil {
	return "", err
}
```

main.go:126-135 — that error becomes a deletion:

```go
if err != nil {
	action := BookmarkAction{Original: b, Action: ActionDelete, Error: err}
```

The tinyurl path is additionally cross-scheme: it POSTs a plaintext `http://` request while README.md:81 claims "Always use HTTPS".</evidence>
<parameter name="impact">Every bookmark whose host is `tinyurl.com` or `is.gd` is destroyed on a non-dry-run pass. The URL is never expanded; instead an error page or a JSON blob is treated as the new URL, fails validation, and the original bookmark is deleted from the user's Pinboard account. This is silent, unrecoverable data loss on exactly the bookmarks the tool advertises it can repair (README.md:4, README.md:16).</impact>
<parameter name="fix">Give each shortener its own decoder and check the status code before using the body.

- Delete the shared `unshortenGeneric` and replace it with per-service functions.
- is.gd: request `https://is.gd/forward.php?format=json&shorturl=<escaped>`, require HTTP 200, `json.Decode` into `struct{ URL string \`json:"url"\`; ErrorCode int \`json:"errorcode"\`; ErrorMessage string \`json:"errormessage"\` }`, return an error when `ErrorCode != 0`, and return `URL`.
- tinyurl: `api-create.php` is the wrong endpoint. Expand a tinyurl by issuing a redirect-suppressed `HEAD` (the same client `urlRedirects` builds) and reading `resp.Location()`; drop `api-create.php` entirely.
- `url.QueryEscape` the short URL in both cases instead of concatenating it onto the endpoint string.
- Reject any expansion result that does not parse via `url.Parse` with a non-empty scheme and host, and return an error rather than a value that will be mistaken for a live URL.

Add table tests over `httptest` servers that return a real is.gd JSON body, an is.gd error body, and a non-200 response, asserting an error rather than a garbage URL in the latter two cases.</fix>
</invoke>

## Evidence

## Impact

## Fix

## Resolution
unshortenGeneric deleted. Replaced with unshortenIsGdImpl (requests format=json, checks the status, decodes url/errorcode/errormessage) and unshortenTinyURLImpl (reads the redirect via redirectClient.Location, dropping the api-create.php create-endpoint entirely). Both route through validExpandedURL, which rejects empty, unparseable, and non-absolute results. expandURL now returns the original URL with a nil error on any expansion failure, so a shortener outage can no longer route a bookmark to deletion. Covered by TestUnshortenIsGdImpl (4 cases), TestUnshortenTinyURLImpl (2), TestValidExpandedURL (5), TestExpandURL_ShortenerFailureKeepsOriginal.
title: unshortenGeneric returns the raw response body as a URL, so every tinyurl and is.gd bookmark is deleted

## Problem

`unshortenBitlyImpl` has three independent defects that compound into silent data loss:

1. It POSTs to `https://api-ssl.bitly.com/v4/expand` with no `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header. Bitly's v4 API rejects unauthenticated calls with 403.
2. It never checks `resp.StatusCode`, so the 403 error body is decoded as if it were a success.
3. It decodes into `struct{ LongURL string }`. Bitly's field is `long_url`; Go's case-insensitive fallback matches `longurl`, not `long_url`, so the field never binds even on a successful response.

The result is `("", nil)` — an empty string with **no error**. `expandURL` returns that, `stats.RecordShortenerExpansion("bitly", err == nil)` records it as a *success*, and `validateURLAccessibility("")` then fails, turning the bookmark into a deletion.</problem>
<parameter name="evidence">main.go:743-764:

```go
func unshortenBitlyImpl(shortURL string) (string, error) {
	resp, err := http.Post(
		"https://api-ssl.bitly.com/v4/expand",
		"application/json",
		strings.NewReader(fmt.Sprintf(`{"short_url": "%s"}`, shortURL)),
	)
	if err != nil { return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to expand bit.ly URL: %w", err) }
	...
	var bitlyResp struct{ LongURL string }
	if err := json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode(&bitlyResp); err != nil { ... }

	return bitlyResp.LongURL, nil
}
```

No auth header, no status check, and `LongURL` cannot match `long_url`.

main.go:720-724 — the empty result is recorded as a successful expansion:

```go
case strings.HasPrefix(cleanedURL, "bit.ly/"):
	result, err := unshortenBitly(shortURL)
	stats.RecordShortenerExpansion("bitly", err == nil)
	return result, err
```

main.go:589-595 then calls `validateURLAccessibility("")`, whose `http.Head("")` errors, and main.go:126-135 converts that error to `ActionDelete`.

The function is entirely unexercised. `go tool cover -func` on the current suite:

```
main.go:743:  unshortenBitlyImpl   0.0%
```

`TestUnshortenBitlyImpl` (main_functions_test.go:330) does not call it — it overwrites the `unshortenBitly` variable with a stub and asserts the stub's own return value.

A secondary defect in the same call: the request body is built with `fmt.Sprintf` into a JSON string literal, so a short URL containing `"` or `\` produces malformed JSON.</evidence>
<parameter name="impact">Every `bit.ly` bookmark is deleted from the user's Pinboard account on a non-dry-run pass, and the statistics report counts each one as a successfully expanded short URL. Because the function returns a nil error, nothing anywhere in the pipeline signals that expansion failed.</impact>
<parameter name="fix">- Build the request with `json.Marshal(map[string]string{"short_url": shortURL})` instead of `fmt.Sprintf`.
- Read a Bitly access token from the environment (e.g. `BITLY_ACCESS_TOKEN`) and set `Authorization: Bearer <token>` via `http.NewRequest` + `client.Do`. When the token is absent, return a sentinel error and have `expandURL` leave the URL untouched rather than treating it as unresolvable.
- Check `resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK` and return an error carrying the status before decoding.
- Tag the field: `struct{ LongURL string \`json:"long_url"\` }`, and return an error when `LongURL` is empty so an unexpanded URL can never be mistaken for a resolved one.
- Guard the shared path regardless of shortener: make `expandAndCheckURL` reject an empty expansion result instead of passing it to `validateURLAccessibility`.

Point `TestUnshortenBitlyImpl` at `unshortenBitlyImpl` against an `httptest` server (inject the base URL as a package variable, as `pinboardAPIEndpoint` already does) and cover 403, malformed-JSON, and `long_url` success cases.</fix>
</invoke>

## Evidence

## Impact

## Fix

## Resolution
unshortenBitlyImpl now sends Authorization: Bearer from BITLY_ACCESS_TOKEN, posts the documented bitlink_id field (built with json.Marshal, not fmt.Sprintf), checks the status, and decodes into a tagged `long_url` field. An absent token returns errNoBitlyToken and expandURL leaves the link untouched. Request and response shapes verified against the Bitly v4 /expand reference. Coverage went 0.0% to exercised: TestUnshortenBitlyImpl_RequiresToken, _SendsBitlinkIDAndReadsLongURL (asserts the header and the bitlink_id body), _RejectsNon200.
title: unshortenBitlyImpl returns an empty URL with a nil error, so every bit.ly bookmark is deleted

## Problem

Pinboard's `URL` data type explicitly allows the schemes `http`, `https`, `javascript`, `mailto`, `ftp`, and `file`. `validateURLAccessibility` reaches every bookmark URL with `http.Head`, which supports only `http` and `https`; every other scheme returns `unsupported protocol scheme`. `expandAndCheckURL` propagates that error and `processBookmark` converts any error into `ActionDelete`.

Nothing in the pipeline distinguishes "this URL is dead" from "this program cannot speak this protocol".</problem>
<parameter name="evidence">Pinboard API documentation, Data Types:

> `URL` — as defined by RFC 3986. Allowed schemes are `http`, `https`, `javascript`, `mailto`, `ftp` and `file`.

Reproduced against Go 1.25.6 (`http.Head` on each allowed scheme):

```
mailto:<email>       err=Head "mailto:<email>": unsupported protocol scheme "mailto"
ftp://ftp.example.com/file       err=Head "ftp://ftp.example.com/file": unsupported protocol scheme "ftp"
file:///etc/hosts                err=Head "file:///etc/hosts": unsupported protocol scheme "file"
javascript:void(0)               err=Head "javascript:void(0)": unsupported protocol scheme "javascript"
```

main.go:618-622:

```go
func validateURLAccessibility(urlString, context string) error {
	resp, err := http.Head(urlString)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("failed to check %s: %w", context, err)
	}
```

main.go:126-135 — every error from that path becomes a deletion:

```go
if err != nil {
	action := BookmarkAction{Original: b, Action: ActionDelete, Error: err}
	stats.RecordAction(action)
	return action
}
```

`javascript:` URLs are how Pinboard stores bookmarklets, so the saved-bookmarklet case is hit too.</evidence>
<parameter name="impact">Every non-HTTP bookmark in the account — saved bookmarklets, `mailto:` contacts, `ftp:` and `file:` links — is deleted on the first non-dry-run pass. These are valid, supported Pinboard bookmarks that the tool has no way to check, and it destroys them rather than skipping them. Unrecoverable without a Pinboard backup.</impact>
<parameter name="fix">Skip what the tool cannot verify instead of deleting it. In `processBookmark`, before any network work:

```go
parsed, err := url.Parse(b.URL)
if err != nil || (parsed.Scheme != "http" && parsed.Scheme != "https") {
	action := BookmarkAction{Original: b, Action: ActionNoChange}
	stats.RecordAction(action)
	return action
}
```

Separately, `ActionDelete` must not be the catch-all for every error. Distinguish the two cases:

- A definite 4xx from `validateURLAccessibility` — a dead link, delete.
- A transport error (DNS failure, TLS failure, timeout, unsupported scheme) — unknown, leave alone and count it as skipped.

Give `expandAndCheckURL` a typed error (e.g. `errDeadLink` vs `errUnverifiable`) and have `processBookmark` delete only on `errors.Is(err, errDeadLink)`. Add a `Skipped` counter to `Statistics` and print it, so unverifiable bookmarks are visible rather than silent.

Add a test asserting `processBookmark(Bookmark{URL: "mailto:<email>"}, ...)` returns `ActionNoChange`.</fix>
</invoke>

## Evidence

## Impact

## Fix

## Resolution
Added isCheckableURL, which processBookmark applies before any network work; non-http(s) bookmarks are recorded via recordSkip and left untouched. Introduced errDeadLink vs errUnverifiable: processBookmark deletes only on errors.Is(err, errDeadLink), so transport failures, timeouts, and undialable schemes now skip instead. Added a Skipped counter, printed in the ACTIONS block. Covered by TestIsCheckableURL, TestProcessBookmark_UndialableSchemeIsSkipped (asserts Skipped==4 and ActionDelete==0), TestValidateURLAccessibility_TransportFailureIsUnverifiable.
title: Bookmarks with mailto:, ftp:, file:, or javascript: URLs are deleted because http.Head cannot dial them

## Problem

`main` reads `PINBOARD_API_TOKEN` from the environment and passes it as the *default value* of the `-token` flag. `flag.PrintDefaults` renders any non-zero default into the usage text, so `pinboard-checker -h` prints the live API token verbatim.</problem>
<parameter name="evidence">main.go:70-71:

```go
apiTokenEnv, _ := os.LookupEnv(tokenName)
apiToken := flag.String("token", apiTokenEnv, "Pinboard API token")
```

Reproduced with a placeholder token in the environment:

```
$ PINBOARD_API_TOKEN='ivuorinen:AAAA***1234' go run . -h
Usage of pinboard-checker:
  ...
  -token string
    	Pinboard API token (default "ivuorinen:AAAA***1234")
```

(the token above is a throwaway value created for this reproduction and is redacted here; the real environment value is printed in full)

A Pinboard auth token is `username:TOKEN` and grants full read/write access to the account (Pinboard API docs, Authentication). README.md:67 states "Your Pinboard API token provides full access to your bookmarks."

The exposure is not limited to an interactive `-h`. `flag` also prints defaults on any parse error, so a typo such as `pinboard-checker -dryrun` dumps the token to stderr — into CI logs, shell history captures, and crash reporters. README.md:155-159 documents `-ci` for CI/CD pipelines, where stderr is routinely archived.</evidence>
<parameter name="impact">The account token is written to stdout/stderr on `-h` and on every flag-parse error, landing in CI job logs and terminal scrollback. Anyone with read access to those logs gains full control of the user's bookmarks. This directly contradicts the tool's own documented threat model (README.md:63-72).</impact>
<parameter name="fix">Never make the secret the flag default. Default to the empty string and fall back to the environment after parsing:

```go
apiToken := flag.String("token", "", "Pinboard API token (default: $PINBOARD_API_TOKEN)")
flag.Parse()

token := *apiToken
if token == "" {
	token = os.Getenv(tokenName)
}
if token == "" {
	fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "Error: API token is required (set PINBOARD_API_TOKEN or pass -token)")
	os.Exit(1)
}
```

The usage string then documents the fallback without disclosing the value.

While here: README.md:60 and README.md:102 recommend `pinboard-checker -token=...` on the command line, which leaks the token to the process table and shell history. README.md:71 already says to prefer the environment; drop the `-token` examples or annotate them as discouraged.</fix>
</invoke>

## Evidence

## Impact

## Fix

## Resolution
-token now defaults to "" and the environment is read after flag.Parse, so PrintDefaults has nothing to disclose. Verified: `PINBOARD_API_TOKEN=<redacted> go run . -h` prints `-token string / Pinboard API token (default: $PINBOARD_API_TOKEN)` with no value. Token validation moved into validateFlags, covered by TestValidateFlags. README's token-security section now also warns that the -token flag leaks into shell history and the process table.
title: The API token is printed in plaintext by -h because it is the -token flag's default value

## Problem

`updateBookmark` implements "update" as `posts/add?url=<newURL>&replace=yes`. Pinboard keys bookmarks by URL, so `replace=yes` replaces the bookmark **at the URL being posted**. When `newURL` differs from `action.Original.URL` — the tool's headline feature — this creates a *new* bookmark at the new URL and leaves the original untouched.

The same call also drops every field the tool never read. `Bookmark` only decodes `description`, `href`, `tags`, and `extended`; `posts/all` also returns `time`, `shared`, and `toread`. Because `posts/add` is called without `dt`, `shared`, or `toread`, Pinboard applies its documented defaults to all three.</problem>
<parameter name="evidence">main.go:421-429 — no `dt`, no `shared`, no `toread`, and `url` is the *new* URL:

```go
req := fmt.Sprintf(
	"%s/posts/add?url=%s&description=%s&extended=%s&tags=%s&replace=yes&auth_token=%s",
	pinboardAPIEndpoint,
	url.QueryEscape(newURL),
	url.QueryEscape(titleToUse),
	url.QueryEscape(b.Notes),
	url.QueryEscape(tagsToUse),
	url.QueryEscape(apiToken),
)
```

main.go:273-286 — nothing deletes the old URL:

```go
func applyUpdateAction(action BookmarkAction, apiToken string, dryRun bool) {
	urlToUpdate := action.NewURL
	if urlToUpdate == "" { urlToUpdate = action.Original.URL }
	if !dryRun {
		err := updateBookmark(apiToken, action.Original, urlToUpdate, action.NewTitle, action.NewTags)
```

main.go:27-32 — the fields that are never read and therefore never restored:

```go
type Bookmark struct {
	Title string `json:"description"`
	URL   string `json:"href"`
	Tags  string `json:"tags,omitempty"`
	Notes string `json:"extended,omitempty"`
}
```

Pinboard API documentation, `posts/add`:

> `dt` — creation time for this bookmark. **Defaults to current time.**
> `shared` — Make bookmark public. **Default is "yes"** unless user has enabled the "save all bookmarks as private" user setting, in which case default is "no".
> `toread` — Marks the bookmark as unread. **Default is "no".**

`posts/all` returns `time` on every post (documented example: `time="2005-11-29T20:30:47Z"`).</evidence>
<parameter name="impact">Two distinct losses on every applied update:

1. **Duplication.** A bookmark whose URL was expanded, de-parenthesised, or redirect-followed ends up stored twice — once at the stale URL, once at the new one. README.md:10 and README.md:137 promise the bookmark is "updated"; the stale copy is never removed, so repeated runs accumulate duplicates.
2. **Metadata destruction.** Every updated bookmark has its creation date reset to now (destroying chronological ordering and any `fromdt`/`todt` workflow), its unread flag cleared, and — for accounts not configured private-by-default — a previously private bookmark republished as public. Finding `audit-XXXX` on `.autoTagged` shows this fires on *every untagged bookmark*, not only genuinely changed ones.</impact>
<parameter name="fix">1. Capture the fields before overwriting them. Extend `Bookmark`:

```go
type Bookmark struct {
	Title  string `json:"description"`
	URL    string `json:"href"`
	Tags   string `json:"tags,omitempty"`
	Notes  string `json:"extended,omitempty"`
	Time   string `json:"time,omitempty"`
	Shared string `json:"shared,omitempty"`
	ToRead string `json:"toread,omitempty"`
}
```

and pass them through in `updateBookmark`, building the query with `url.Values` rather than `fmt.Sprintf`:

```go
q := url.Values{}
q.Set("url", newURL)
q.Set("description", titleToUse)
q.Set("extended", b.Notes)
q.Set("tags", tagsToUse)
q.Set("replace", "yes")
if b.Time != "" { q.Set("dt", b.Time) }
if b.Shared != "" { q.Set("shared", b.Shared) }
if b.ToRead != "" { q.Set("toread", b.ToRead) }
q.Set("auth_token", apiToken)
```

2. When the URL actually changes, make it a move: add at the new URL, verify success (see the finding on unchecked `<result code>` bodies), then `deleteBookmark(apiToken, action.Original.URL)`. Add-then-delete in that order so a crash between the two leaves a duplicate rather than nothing. Do not delete when `newURL == Original.URL`.

3. Add a test that drives `applyUpdateAction` against an `httptest` server recording the requests, asserting a `posts/add` with `dt`/`shared`/`toread` preserved followed by a `posts/delete` for the old URL.</fix>
</invoke>

## Evidence

## Impact

## Fix

## Resolution
Bookmark gained Time/Shared/ToRead, and updateBookmark sends them as dt/shared/toread so posts/add cannot re-default the creation date, privacy, or unread flag. Query now built with url.Values instead of fmt.Sprintf. New applyUpdateWrite deletes the stale URL after a successful add when the URL changed, making the update a move rather than a duplicate; the delete never runs before the add lands. Covered by TestUpdateBookmark_PreservesMetadataAndTargetsTheNewURL (asserts dt/shared/toread/replace on the wire), TestApplyUpdateAction_URLChangeRemovesTheOldBookmark (asserts add-then-delete order and the delete target), TestApplyUpdateAction_TitleOnlyDoesNotDelete, TestGetBookmarks_Success.
title: Changing a bookmark's URL creates a duplicate and resets its creation date, privacy, and read-later state

## Problem

Pinboard's API returns XML by default; JSON only when `format=json` is passed. `getBookmarks` passes it. `getSuggestedTags` does not, yet decodes the response with `json.NewDecoder`. Against the real API the decode fails on the first byte of `<suggested>`, so `getSuggestedTags` always returns an error.

Auto-tagging is on by default (`-skip-auto-tags` defaults to false), so this fires for every untagged bookmark in the account.</problem>
<parameter name="evidence">main.go:524-527 — no `format=json`:

```go
apiURL := fmt.Sprintf("%s/posts/suggest?url=%s&auth_token=%s",
	pinboardAPIEndpoint,
	url.QueryEscape(urlStr),
	url.QueryEscape(apiToken))
```

main.go:381-383 — the same file gets it right for the other endpoint:

```go
resp, err := http.Get(fmt.Sprintf("%s/posts/all?auth_token=%s&format=json",
	pinboardAPIEndpoint,
	url.QueryEscape(apiToken)))
```

main.go:550-552 — decoded as JSON regardless:

```go
if err := json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode(&suggestions); err != nil {
	return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to decode tag suggestions JSON: %w", err)
}
```

Pinboard API documentation, Methods:

> Methods return data in XML (default) or JSON format.

Pinboard API documentation, Data Types:

> `format` — the literal string 'json' or 'xml'

The documented `posts/suggest` response is XML:

```xml
<suggested>
    <popular>blog</popular>
    <recommended>weblog</recommended>
</suggested>
```

The test suite cannot catch this: every `posts/suggest` test serves a hand-written JSON body from an `httptest` server (main_test.go:201, apply_functions_test.go:299), so the fixture asserts a format the production endpoint is never asked for.

Note that `posts/suggest` returns the popular and recommended sets as *siblings* under one `<suggested>` element. `collectTagsFromSuggestions` (main.go:566-579) only ever indexes `suggestions[0]`, so once the format is fixed the shape of the decoded JSON must be re-verified against a live response before assuming both sets land in one element.</evidence>
<parameter name="impact">The "Auto-Tagging" feature advertised at README.md:20 and README.md:133-135 has never worked against the real Pinboard API. Every untagged bookmark still pays for the attempt: `getSuggestedTags` calls `waitForRateLimit` first, so each one blocks the global 3-second rate limiter before failing. On an account with 500 untagged bookmarks that is 25 minutes of wall clock spent on requests that cannot succeed, reported to the user as "Tags fetched: 0 (500 failed)".</impact>
<parameter name="fix">Add the parameter and build the query with `url.Values` so it cannot be forgotten again:

```go
q := url.Values{}
q.Set("url", urlStr)
q.Set("auth_token", apiToken)
q.Set("format", "json")
apiURL := pinboardAPIEndpoint + "/posts/suggest?" + q.Encode()
```

Then confirm the decoded shape against a real response before trusting `collectTagsFromSuggestions`: capture one live `posts/suggest?format=json` body, commit it as a testdata fixture, and drive the existing tests from that file instead of a hand-written literal. If popular and recommended arrive as two separate array elements, `collectTagsFromSuggestions` must iterate all elements rather than only `suggestions[0]`.

Apply the same treatment to `posts/add` and `posts/delete`, which also omit `format` (see the finding on unchecked result codes).</fix>
</invoke>

## Evidence

## Impact

## Fix

## Resolution
All five Pinboard calls now go through pinboardGet, which sets format=json and auth_token centrally so no site can omit either. collectTagsFromSuggestions iterates every element of the response rather than only suggestions[0], so popular and recommended are both collected whether Pinboard returns them as one element or two; both shapes are covered by TestGetSuggestedTags. TestGetSuggestedTags_RequestsJSON asserts format=json is on the wire, which is the regression guard the previous hand-written fixture could not provide.
title: getSuggestedTags omits format=json, so Pinboard returns XML and auto-tagging never works

## Problem

Every outbound request uses `http.Get`, `http.Head`, or `http.Post`, all of which route through `http.DefaultClient`. `http.DefaultClient` has a zero `Timeout`, meaning no deadline at all. The one custom client the code builds (`urlRedirects`, main.go:676) sets `CheckRedirect` but also leaves `Timeout` unset.

A server that accepts the TCP connection and then never responds holds the calling goroutine forever.</problem>
<parameter name="evidence">Every request site, none of which sets a deadline:

```
main.go:381  http.Get(...)     getBookmarks
main.go:430  http.Get(req)     updateBookmark
main.go:452  http.Get(...)     deleteBookmark
main.go:474  http.Get(urlString)   getPageTitle
main.go:529  http.Get(apiURL)  getSuggestedTags
main.go:619  http.Head(urlString)  validateURLAccessibility
main.go:650  http.Head(updatedURL) fixParenthesesSuffix
main.go:744  http.Post(...)    unshortenBitlyImpl
main.go:767  http.Get(...)     unshortenGeneric
```

main.go:676-680 — the only custom client, also without a timeout:

```go
client := &http.Client{
	CheckRedirect: func(_ *http.Request, _ []*http.Request) error {
		return http.ErrUseLastResponse
	},
}
```

The blocked goroutine holds a worker slot for the whole program lifetime. main.go:233-236:

```go
sem <- struct{}{}
go func(b Bookmark) {
	defer wg.Done()
	defer func() { <-sem }()
```

With the default `-workers 10`, ten such hosts exhaust the semaphore and the dispatch loop blocks on `sem <- struct{}{}` forever. There is no `context`, no `signal.NotifyContext`, and no overall deadline anywhere in the program, so the process cannot make progress and cannot be interrupted cleanly.

README.md:219-222 acknowledges the symptom but describes behaviour the code does not implement:

> ### Timeouts
> Some URLs may timeout if the target server is slow to respond. These will be marked as errors and can be deleted or skipped based on your preferences.

There is no timeout to mark as an error, and no "skip" preference exists.</evidence>
<parameter name="impact">A single unresponsive bookmark host stalls one of ten workers permanently; ten of them stall the whole run with no output, no progress-bar movement, and no exit. Because bookmark collections are exactly where long-abandoned hosts accumulate, this is likely rather than theoretical. The user must kill the process, and any work the second phase would have applied is lost.</impact>
<parameter name="fix">Build one shared client with an explicit timeout and use it everywhere instead of the `http.DefaultClient` helpers:

```go
// httpClient bounds every outbound request. http.DefaultClient has no timeout,
// so an unresponsive bookmark host would otherwise hold a worker slot forever
// and, at ten such hosts, deadlock the dispatch loop.
var httpClient = &http.Client{Timeout: 15 * time.Second}

// redirectClient reports the first redirect instead of following it, and
// inherits the same deadline.
var redirectClient = &http.Client{
	Timeout: 15 * time.Second,
	CheckRedirect: func(_ *http.Request, _ []*http.Request) error {
		return http.ErrUseLastResponse
	},
}
```

Replace all nine call sites with `httpClient.Get` / `httpClient.Head` / `httpClient.Post` and main.go:676 with `redirectClient`. Expose the value as a `-timeout` flag so slow-but-live hosts can be accommodated.

Timeouts must not become deletions — route them through the `errUnverifiable` path described in the finding on non-HTTP schemes, so a slow host is skipped rather than destroyed.

Then correct README.md:219-222 to describe the real behaviour, including the default timeout value.</fix>
</invoke>

## Evidence

## Impact

## Fix

## Resolution
Replaced every http.Get/Head/Post package helper with a shared httpClient (and redirectClient for the redirect probe), both carrying a 15s default timeout exposed as -timeout. setHTTPTimeout applies the flag after parsing; validateFlags rejects a non-positive value. Timeouts surface as errUnverifiable, so a slow host is skipped rather than deleted. README's Troubleshooting section rewritten to describe the real behavior instead of the timeout handling that did not exist.

## Problem

`-workers` is read straight into `make(chan struct{}, workers)` with no validation. A zero value produces an unbuffered channel, and the dispatch loop sends into it *before* starting the goroutine that would receive — so the send blocks with no possible receiver. A negative value panics inside `make`.</problem>
<parameter name="evidence">main.go:77 — no bounds:

```go
workers := flag.Int("workers", 10, "Number of concurrent workers for parallel processing")
```

main.go:229-236 — the send precedes the goroutine that drains it:

```go
sem := make(chan struct{}, workers)

for _, bookmark := range bookmarks {
	wg.Add(1)
	sem <- struct{}{}
	go func(b Bookmark) {
		defer wg.Done()
		defer func() { <-sem }()
```

Reproduced against Go 1.25.6 with the same construction:

```
workers=10  -> send proceeded
workers=1   -> send proceeded
workers=0   -> BLOCKED (no receiver; dispatch loop deadlocks)
workers=-1  -> PANIC: makechan: size out of range
```

`-workers 0` is not an exotic input: it is the natural way to express "no concurrency", and it is what a shell expands `-workers $N` to when `N` is unset.

The whole function is untested — `go tool cover -func` on the current suite:

```
main.go:217:  processBookmarksParallel   0.0%
```

so no test exercises any worker count, valid or not.</evidence>
<parameter name="impact">`pinboard-checker -workers 0` hangs forever after fetching bookmarks, with the progress bar showing 0 of N and no error. `-workers -1` crashes with an unhandled runtime panic and a stack trace instead of a usage message. Neither failure names the flag that caused it, so the operator has nothing to act on.</impact>
<parameter name="fix">Validate immediately after `flag.Parse()`, alongside the existing token check:

```go
if *workers < 1 {
	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Error: -workers must be at least 1, got %d\n", *workers)
	os.Exit(1)
}
```

An upper bound is worth adding too — every worker holds an open connection, and values in the thousands will exhaust file descriptors before they help. Cap at something defensible (e.g. 100) and say so in the message.

Add a test for `processBookmarksParallel` — currently at 0% coverage — covering `workers = 1`, `workers` greater than `len(bookmarks)`, and an empty bookmark slice, asserting that the returned action count matches the input count in each case. That test is what would have caught this and is missing for the one function in the file that manages concurrency.

Document the accepted range in README.md:114-121, which does not list `-workers` at all despite it being a supported flag.</fix>
</invoke>

## Evidence

## Impact

## Fix

## Resolution
validateFlags rejects -workers outside 1..maxWorkers (100) with a message naming the flag, before any channel is made. Covered by TestValidateFlags (zero, negative, and over-cap cases). processBookmarksParallel, previously at 0.0% coverage, now has TestProcessBookmarksParallel exercising one worker, more workers than bookmarks, and an empty slice. -workers and its range are documented in README's Options list.

## Problem

When `getBookmarks` fails, `main` prints a message and `return`s. Returning from `main` exits with status 0. Nothing else in the program sets a non-zero exit either: update and delete failures are swallowed (see the finding on silently dropped write errors), so the only non-zero exit in the entire binary is the missing-token check.

`main` also assigns `stats.TotalBookmarks` from the result slice *before* checking the error, reading a value the failed call did not produce.</problem>
<parameter name="evidence">main.go:85-94:

```go
stats.FetchBookmarksStart = time.Now()
bookmarks, err := getBookmarks(*apiToken)
stats.FetchBookmarksDuration = time.Since(stats.FetchBookmarksStart)
stats.TotalBookmarks = len(bookmarks)

if err != nil {
	fmt.Println("Error fetching bookmarks:", err)

	return
}
```

The `return` is the only exit path for this branch, and `main` has no deferred exit-code handling. Compare main.go:80-83, which does it correctly for the token:

```go
if *apiToken == "" {
	fmt.Println("Error: API token is required")
	os.Exit(1)
}
```

The error message also goes to stdout via `fmt.Println` rather than stderr, so it is indistinguishable from normal output in a piped log.

This matters specifically because the tool ships a CI mode. README.md:155-159:

> ### Run in CI/CD pipeline
> ```bash
> pinboard-checker -ci
> ```

and main.go:109-112 suppresses the statistics block entirely under `-ci`, so a CI run that fails to authenticate produces one line on stdout and exit code 0.</evidence>
<parameter name="impact">A scheduled `pinboard-checker -ci` job whose token has been revoked, or which is being rate-limited with a 429, exits green. The pipeline records a successful maintenance run while zero bookmarks were examined, and the failure is only discoverable by reading the job's stdout. This can persist indefinitely without anyone noticing the tool stopped working.</impact>
<parameter name="fix">Exit non-zero and write errors to stderr:

```go
bookmarks, err := getBookmarks(*apiToken)
stats.FetchBookmarksDuration = time.Since(stats.FetchBookmarksStart)
if err != nil {
	fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "Error fetching bookmarks:", err)
	os.Exit(1)
}
stats.TotalBookmarks = len(bookmarks)
```

Note the reordering: `stats.TotalBookmarks` must be assigned after the error check, not from the slice a failed call returned.

Beyond the fetch, give the run an overall verdict. Track applied-write failures in `Statistics` (there is already a `TotalErrors` field, main.go:51, that is incremented but never read or printed) and exit 1 when any write failed, so a partially-failed run is visible to CI. Print the failure count in the statistics block, and print it under `-ci` too — suppressing the progress bar should not suppress the outcome.

Route the existing `fmt.Println` error paths at main.go:81 and main.go:91 to `os.Stderr` so logs can separate diagnostics from results.</fix>
</invoke>

## Evidence

## Impact

## Fix

## Resolution
Extracted run(), which returns an exit code that main passes to os.Exit, so os.Exit is reached from one place after deferred cleanup. A failed fetch returns 1; a run with any rejected write returns 1 via stats.ApplyErrorCount(). stats.TotalBookmarks is now assigned after the error check rather than from the slice a failed call returned. All error output moved to stderr. The failure count prints even under -ci. README's CI/CD example documents the exit-code contract.
title: A failed bookmark fetch exits with status 0, so CI pipelines report success on a run that did nothing

## Problem

Ten of the twelve test functions in `apply_functions_test.go` call the function under test and then end. They contain no `if`, no comparison, and no `t.Error`. They pass unconditionally unless the code panics, and would continue to pass if `applyUpdateAction`, `applyDeleteAction`, and `applyBookmarkActions` were replaced with empty bodies.

Two further tests elsewhere are tautological in a different way: they overwrite the function-pointer variable with a stub and then assert the stub's own return value.</problem>
<parameter name="evidence">Assertion-free tests, all of `apply_functions_test.go`:

```
TestApplyUpdateAction_DryRun       :11
TestApplyUpdateAction_URLOnly      :32
TestApplyUpdateAction_TitleOnly    :56
TestApplyDeleteAction_DryRun       :80
TestApplyDeleteAction_Success      :95
TestApplyDeleteAction_Error        :119
TestApplyDeleteAction_NonVerbose   :143
TestApplyBookmarkActions_NoActions :167
TestApplyBookmarkActions_WithActions :185
TestApplyBookmarkActions_CIMode    :224
```

The pattern, and the comment acknowledging it (apply_functions_test.go:25-28):

```go
	// Test dry run - should not make actual API calls
	applyUpdateAction(action, "test-token", true)

	// In dry run, updates counter should not increment
	// Since we can't easily check without modifying global state, just ensure no panic
}
```

Tautological stubs — `TestUnshortenBitlyImpl` (main_functions_test.go:330) is named for `unshortenBitlyImpl` but never calls it:

```go
	unshortenBitly = func(_ string) (string, error) {
		return expectedURL, nil
	}

	result, err := unshortenBitly("https://bit.ly/test")
	if result != expectedURL { ... }
```

Confirmed by coverage — the function the test is named after is never entered:

```
$ go tool cover -func=cov.out
main.go:743:  unshortenBitlyImpl        0.0%
main.go:217:  processBookmarksParallel  0.0%
```

Both tests also spin up an `httptest` server that no code path ever contacts (main_functions_test.go:333-341, main_test.go:13-18).

`TestExpandURL_Bitly` (main_test.go:11) has the same shape. `TestFetchTitleIfNeeded` and `TestFetchTagsIfNeeded` (main_functions_test.go:86, :125) declare a `wantEmpty` field that is `true` in every case, so the non-empty branch is never asserted.

Total suite coverage is 78.0% — the number is produced largely by tests that execute code without checking it.</evidence>
<parameter name="impact">The two functions that perform every destructive Pinboard write, `applyUpdateAction` and `applyDeleteAction`, have no behavioural test at all despite reporting 94.1% and 100% statement coverage. The suite cannot detect a regression that stops issuing requests, issues them to the wrong URL, or miscounts successes — and it did not detect any of the correctness defects filed in this audit. `processBookmarksParallel`, the only concurrent code in the program, is at 0%. The coverage figure actively misleads: it certifies as tested the code least verified.</impact>
<parameter name="fix">Assert on observable effects rather than on absence of panic. All three functions are observable through the HTTP requests they issue and the counters they bump.

1. Record requests in the `httptest` handler and assert on them:

```go
var got []string
server := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	got = append(got, r.URL.Path+"?"+r.URL.RawQuery)
	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
}))
...
applyUpdateAction(action, "test-token", true)
if len(got) != 0 {
	t.Errorf("dry run issued %d requests, want 0: %v", len(got), got)
}
```

That single assertion is what makes `TestApplyUpdateAction_DryRun` meaningful, and it is exactly the check the comment at :27-28 says was skipped.

2. Make the counters assertable. `stats` is a package-level singleton (main.go:59-64), which is why the author gave up. Add a constructor and reset it per test:

```go
func newStatistics() *Statistics {
	return &Statistics{
		ShortURLsExpanded: make(map[string]int),
		ShortURLsFailed:   make(map[string]int),
		StatusCodes:       make(map[string]map[int]int),
	}
}
```

then `stats = newStatistics()` at the top of each test, asserting `stats.UpdatesPerformed` and `stats.DeletionsPerformed` afterwards.

3. Point `TestUnshortenBitlyImpl` and `TestExpandURL_Bitly` at the real implementations (see the `unshortenBitlyImpl` finding for the injectable-endpoint change they need), and delete the unused `httptest` servers in both.

4. Give `TestFetchTitleIfNeeded` and `TestFetchTagsIfNeeded` at least one `wantEmpty: false` case, or drop the field.

5. Add the missing `processBookmarksParallel` test described in the `-workers` finding.</fix>
</invoke>

## Evidence

## Impact

## Fix

## Resolution
apply_functions_test.go rewritten: every test now asserts on the requests issued (via a new recordingServer that captures path and query) or on the counters moved. Dry-run tests assert zero requests — the check the old comment said could not be made. Added newStatistics() plus a resetStats(t) helper so the stats singleton is per-test and assertable. TestUnshortenBitlyImpl and TestExpandURL_Bitly now drive the real implementations rather than a stub asserting itself; unused httptest servers removed. fetchTitleIfNeeded/fetchTagsIfNeeded tables gained the non-empty cases their wantEmpty field never exercised. Coverage 78.0% to 83.1%, with processBookmarksParallel and unshortenBitlyImpl no longer at 0.0%.
title: Ten test functions contain no assertions and pass unless the code panics, inflating coverage to 78% without verifying behavior

## Problem

Three tests reach the public internet instead of an `httptest` server. Two of them additionally discard the result, with a comment stating that any outcome is acceptable — so they assert nothing whatever the network does.

A fourth test reaches `api.pinboard.in` indirectly: `TestProcessBookmark_URLError` leaves `skipAutoTags` at whatever the previous test left it and calls `processBookmark`, which calls `getSuggestedTags` against the unmocked `pinboardAPIEndpoint` — after blocking on the global 3-second rate limiter.</problem>
<parameter name="evidence">main_functions_test.go:373-398 — live calls, no assertions:

```go
func TestExpandURL_TinyURL(t *testing.T) {
	...
	// This will fail because we can't easily mock the tinyurl API
	// but it will increase coverage of the expandURL function
	_, err := expandURL("https://tinyurl.com/test", false)
	// We expect an error because the actual API call will fail
	// If no error, that's also acceptable - it means the URL was processed
	_ = err // Ignore error as both outcomes are acceptable
}

func TestExpandURL_IsGd(t *testing.T) {
	...
	_, err := expandURL("https://is.gd/test", false)
	_ = err // Ignore error as both outcomes are acceptable
}
```

`TestExpandURL_TinyURL` also creates an `httptest` server (:375-381) that the live call never contacts.

main_functions_test.go:483-503 — `processBookmark` with `pinboardAPIEndpoint` left at its production default (main.go:25, `https://api.pinboard.in/v1`):

```go
func TestProcessBookmark_URLError(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	...
	action := processBookmark(bookmark, "test-token")
```

`processBookmark` → `fetchTagsIfNeeded` → `getSuggestedTags` → `waitForRateLimit()` (main.go:522) then `http.Get` against the real host, sending `auth_token=test-token`.

Measured cost, on a suite whose entire subject is 1,117 lines:

```
$ go test -race -count=1 ./...
ok  github.com/ivuorinen/pinboard-checker  58.722s
```

The CI job runs exactly this (.github/workflows/go.yml:27-28):

```yaml
    - name: Test
      run: go test -v ./...
```

The comment "we can't easily mock the tinyurl API" is not accurate — `pinboardAPIEndpoint` (main.go:25) and `unshortenBitly` (main.go:741) already exist as seams for precisely this, and `TestUnshortenGeneric` (main_functions_test.go:310) already passes an `httptest` URL as the endpoint argument.</evidence>
<parameter name="impact">The suite fails or hangs without network access, and depends on three third-party services staying reachable and behaving unchanged — any of which can turn CI red for reasons unrelated to the code. Runtime is 58 seconds for a 2,800-line repository, almost all of it spent blocking on the rate limiter and remote hosts. The two shortener tests exist only to move the coverage number; they cannot fail, which is why they did not catch the `unshortenGeneric` defect filed as critical in this audit. Sending `auth_token=test-token` to a third party's production API on every CI run is also gratuitous traffic against a service whose documented rate limit the suite is ignoring.</impact>
<parameter name="fix">1. Introduce endpoint variables for the two shorteners, mirroring `pinboardAPIEndpoint`:

```go
var (
	tinyURLEndpoint = "https://tinyurl.com"
	isGdEndpoint    = "https://is.gd"
)
```

Have `expandURL` build its URLs from those, and point the tests at `httptest` servers. Then assert on the returned URL rather than discarding the error.

2. Fix `TestProcessBookmark_URLError` to set `skipAutoTags = true` and `skipTitles = true` explicitly, or better, override `pinboardAPIEndpoint` for the duration. It must not depend on state a previous test happened to leave behind. Note it currently declares `t.Parallel()` while reading globals other tests mutate; once it sets them itself it must drop `t.Parallel()`, as the neighbouring tests already do.

3. Delete the unused `httptest` server at main_functions_test.go:375-381.

4. Add a guard so this cannot regress: a `TestMain` that fails fast if `pinboardAPIEndpoint` still points at `api.pinboard.in` when a test finishes, or run CI tests with a `-short` gate on any test that needs the network.

Once the live calls are gone the suite should run in well under a second, since the only remaining 3-second waits come from `waitForRateLimit` against local servers — consider making the ticker interval a variable so tests can shorten it.</fix>
</invoke>

## Evidence

## Impact

## Fix

## Resolution
No test reaches the network any more. isGdEndpoint and bitlyEndpoint joined pinboardAPIEndpoint as injectable seams; the tinyurl path is driven by pointing the expander at an httptest server. The assertion-free TestExpandURL_TinyURL/_IsGd (which discarded the error as "both outcomes acceptable") are gone. TestProcessBookmark tests set the skip flags explicitly instead of inheriting whatever ran before, removing the live api.pinboard.in call. Added TestMain shortening the rate-limiter interval. Suite runtime 58.7s to 1.1s under -race.

## Problem

`urlRedirects` reads `resp.Header.Get("Location")` and returns it verbatim as the new bookmark URL. RFC 7231 permits `Location` to be a relative reference, and many servers send one (`/new-path`, `../other`). Stored verbatim, that is not a usable bookmark.

The same function recognises only 301 and 302. HTTP 303, 307, and 308 are redirects too; 308 in particular is the standard permanent redirect for non-GET-safe moves and is common on sites that have migrated to HTTPS.</problem>
<parameter name="evidence">main.go:692-703:

```go
if resp.StatusCode == http.StatusMovedPermanently || resp.StatusCode == http.StatusFound {
	redirectURL := resp.Header.Get("Location")
	if redirectURL != "" {
		stats.IncrementRedirects()
		...
		return redirectURL, nil
	}
}
```

A relative `Location` flows straight into `validateURLAccessibility` (main.go:611):

```go
redirectedURL, err := urlRedirects(fixedURL, verbose)
if err != nil { return "", err }
if err := validateURLAccessibility(redirectedURL, "redirected URL"); err != nil {
	return "", err
}
```

`http.Head("/new-path")` fails with `unsupported protocol scheme ""`, so the bookmark is routed to `ActionDelete` (main.go:126-135) rather than updated.

`TestUrlRedirects` (main_test.go:52) only serves an absolute `Location`, so neither the relative case nor 303/307/308 is covered.

Go's standard library already solves this: `(*http.Response).Location()` resolves the header against the request URL and returns an error when the header is absent.</evidence>
<parameter name="impact">A bookmark on a site using relative redirects is deleted rather than updated — the same data-loss outcome as the unsupported-scheme finding, reached by a different path. Sites redirecting with 308 or 307 are silently left un-updated, so the "Following redirects to final destinations" feature (README.md:5) misses a large and growing fraction of real redirects.</impact>
<parameter name="fix">Use `resp.Location()`, which resolves relative references against the request URL, and cover the full redirect set:

```go
switch resp.StatusCode {
case http.StatusMovedPermanently, http.StatusFound, http.StatusSeeOther,
	http.StatusTemporaryRedirect, http.StatusPermanentRedirect:
	// Location may be relative; resp.Location resolves it against the request URL.
	// Returning the raw header would store "/new-path" as the bookmark URL.
	target, err := resp.Location()
	if err != nil {
		return urlString, nil //nolint:nilerr // no usable Location: leave the URL alone
	}
	stats.IncrementRedirects()
	if verbose {
		fmt.Printf("Redirected URL updated: '%s' -> '%s'\n", urlString, target)
	}

	return target.String(), nil
}

return urlString, nil
```

Consider also following redirect chains to a fixed point (with a hop limit, e.g. 5) rather than taking only the first hop — a shortener behind a shortener currently resolves one level and stores an intermediate URL.

Extend `TestUrlRedirects` into a table covering 301, 302, 303, 307, 308, an absent `Location`, and a relative `Location` such as `/final`, asserting the resolved absolute URL in the last case.</fix>
</invoke>

## Evidence

## Impact

## Fix

## Resolution
urlRedirects now uses resp.Location(), which resolves a relative Location against the request URL, and handles 303/307/308 alongside 301/302. A redirect status with no usable Location leaves the URL unchanged. Covered by TestUrlRedirects across all five statuses plus a relative-Location case asserting the resolved absolute URL, and TestUrlRedirects_NoRedirect asserting the counter stays at zero.

## Problem

`processBookmark` calls `expandAndCheckURL`, then unconditionally calls `fetchTitleIfNeeded` and `fetchTagsIfNeeded`, and only *afterwards* checks the error. When the URL check failed, both fetches still run — and because `expandAndCheckURL` returns `""` on error, both fall back to `b.URL`, the URL just proven unreachable.

One of the two, `fetchTagsIfNeeded`, blocks on the global 3-second rate limiter before issuing its request.</problem>
<parameter name="evidence">main.go:120-135:

```go
newURL, err := expandAndCheckURL(b.URL, verbose)

newTitle := fetchTitleIfNeeded(b, newURL)
newTags := fetchTagsIfNeeded(b, apiToken, newURL)

// If there was an error checking the URL, mark for deletion
if err != nil {
	action := BookmarkAction{
		Original: b,
		Action:   ActionDelete,
		Error:    err,
	}
```

main.go:587-592 — the error path returns an empty string, not the original URL:

```go
expandedURL, err := expandURL(url, verbose)
if err != nil {
	return "", err
}
```

so main.go:174-177 falls back to the dead URL:

```go
urlToFetch := b.URL
if newURL != "" {
	urlToFetch = newURL
}
```

main.go:522 — the tag fetch takes the rate limiter first:

```go
func getSuggestedTags(apiToken, urlStr string) (string, error) {
	waitForRateLimit()
```

The results are discarded: `newTitle` and `newTags` are computed but never read on the `err != nil` branch, which constructs `BookmarkAction` with only `Original`, `Action`, and `Error`.

The wasted work also corrupts the report — `stats.RecordTitleFetch` (main.go:180) and `stats.RecordTagFetch` (main.go:204) record a failure for each dead bookmark, so "Titles fetched: N failed" counts bookmarks that were never candidates for a title.</evidence>
<parameter name="impact">Every dead bookmark costs two extra HTTP requests plus a full 3-second rate-limiter slot, none of which can affect the outcome. An account with 200 dead links spends an additional 10 minutes of wall clock producing values that are discarded, and reports 200 spurious title/tag fetch failures in the statistics block. The rate limiter is global and mutex-guarded (main.go:368-372), so the delay is serialised across all workers rather than absorbed by concurrency.</impact>
<parameter name="fix">Check the error before doing any further work:

```go
newURL, err := expandAndCheckURL(b.URL, verbose)
if err != nil {
	action := BookmarkAction{Original: b, Action: ActionDelete, Error: err}
	stats.RecordAction(action)

	return action
}

newTitle := fetchTitleIfNeeded(b, newURL)
newTags := fetchTagsIfNeeded(b, apiToken, newURL)
```

This is a pure reordering — the two fetch results are already unused on the error path — so it changes no outcome, only the work done to reach it.

`TestProcessBookmark_URLError` (main_functions_test.go:483) already exercises this path and is the test that currently triggers a live `api.pinboard.in` call; the reordering removes that call as a side effect. Add an assertion there that no suggest request was issued, using a recording `httptest` handler.</fix>
</invoke>

## Evidence

## Impact

## Fix

## Resolution
processBookmark now checks the expandAndCheckURL error and returns before fetchTitleIfNeeded/fetchTagsIfNeeded, so a dead bookmark no longer costs two discarded requests and a rate-limiter slot, and no longer inflates the title/tag failure counts. Covered by TestProcessBookmark_SkipsFetchesForDeadLinks, which asserts TitlesFailed and TagsFailed stay at zero for a 404 bookmark.

## Problem

Both apply functions handle a write error by printing it — but only when `verbose` is true. Without `-verbose` the error is dropped entirely: no message, no counter, no effect on the exit code. `applyUpdateAction` expresses this in a way that also makes the intent hard to read: the error branch is fused into the success branch's `else if`.

`Statistics` already carries a `TotalErrors` field for exactly this, but it is only incremented for URL-check failures and is never printed anywhere.</problem>
<parameter name="evidence">main.go:279-286:

```go
if !dryRun {
	err := updateBookmark(apiToken, action.Original, urlToUpdate, action.NewTitle, action.NewTags)
	if err != nil && verbose {
		fmt.Printf("Error updating %s: %v\n", action.Original.URL, err)
	} else if err == nil {
		stats.IncrementUpdates()
	}
}
```

With `err != nil` and `verbose == false`, neither branch runs: the first is false, and `else if err == nil` is false. The error simply vanishes.

main.go:312-319 — same shape in `applyDeleteAction`:

```go
err := deleteBookmark(apiToken, action.Original.URL)
if err != nil {
	if verbose {
		fmt.Printf("Error deleting %s: %v\n", action.Original.URL, err)
	}

	return
}
```

statistics.go:50-51 — the field that should record this:

```go
	// Errors
	TotalErrors int
```

Its only write is statistics.go:72-75, for deletions decided during processing:

```go
case ActionDelete:
	s.ActionDelete++
	s.TotalErrors++
```

and it appears in none of the eight `print*` methods (statistics.go:145-315), so it is dead state.

The tests cannot detect any of this: `TestApplyDeleteAction_Error` (apply_functions_test.go:119) serves HTTP 500 and then asserts nothing at all.</evidence>
<parameter name="impact">A non-verbose run — the default, and the mode README.md:155-159 recommends for CI — reports "Updates performed: 40" when 40 were attempted and, say, 12 failed with 429s. The operator sees a clean statistics block and a zero exit code for a run that silently failed to apply a quarter of its changes. Because the failures are neither counted nor logged, there is no way to discover this short of diffing the account by hand.</impact>
<parameter name="fix">Always record the failure; gate only the message on `verbose`.

```go
if !dryRun {
	err := updateBookmark(apiToken, action.Original, urlToUpdate, action.NewTitle, action.NewTags)
	switch {
	case err != nil:
		stats.RecordApplyError()
		if verbose {
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Error updating %s: %v\n", action.Original.URL, err)
		}
	default:
		stats.IncrementUpdates()
	}
}
```

Apply the same shape in `applyDeleteAction`.

Add the counter and surface it:

```go
// RecordApplyError counts a write that Pinboard rejected. Without it a
// non-verbose run reports only successes and exits 0, so a partially
// failed run is indistinguishable from a clean one.
func (s *Statistics) RecordApplyError() {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	s.ApplyErrors++
}
```

Print `ApplyErrors` in `printAPIOperations`, print it even under `-ci`, and give `TotalErrors` the same treatment or delete the field. Have `main` exit non-zero when `ApplyErrors > 0`, per the finding on exit codes.

Then make `TestApplyDeleteAction_Error` assert `stats.ApplyErrors == 1` — it already sets up the 500 response and just needs the check.</fix>
</invoke>

## Evidence

## Impact

## Fix

## Resolution
Write failures are now always recorded via stats.RecordApplyError(); only the message is gated on -verbose, through a new reportApplyError helper. Added the ApplyErrors counter and ApplyErrorCount(), printed in the API OPERATIONS block as "Writes rejected" and used by run() to exit non-zero. The dead TotalErrors field was removed rather than wired in — it duplicated ActionDelete exactly; statistics_test.go's assertion was replaced with one checking that a delete does not touch the other action counters. Covered by TestApplyUpdateAction_CountsFailureWhenNotVerbose and TestApplyDeleteAction_CountsFailure.

## Problem

The rate limiter is a fixed 3-second ticker with no feedback from the server. Nothing anywhere inspects `http.StatusTooManyRequests`, and nothing widens the interval when Pinboard pushes back. The Pinboard documentation states this requirement directly.

The fixed interval is also wrong for one endpoint: `posts/all` is limited to once every five minutes, not three seconds, and `getBookmarks` takes the same 3-second ticket as everything else.</problem>
<parameter name="evidence">main.go:56 and main.go:368-372 — a fixed ticker, no adaptation:

```go
rateLimiter    = time.NewTicker(3 * time.Second)
rateLimiterMux sync.Mutex
...
func waitForRateLimit() {
	rateLimiterMux.Lock()
	defer rateLimiterMux.Unlock()
	<-rateLimiter.C
}
```

Pinboard API documentation, Rate Limits:

> API requests are limited to one call per user every three seconds, except for the following:
> - `posts/all` - once every five minutes
> - `posts/recent` - once every minute
>
> Make sure your API clients check for `429 Too Many Requests` server errors and back off appropriately. If possible, keep doubling the interval between requests until you stop receiving errors.

No occurrence of `429` or `StatusTooManyRequests` exists in the codebase. A 429 is instead handled as an ordinary failure at each call site:

- `updateBookmark` (main.go:439) returns `"update failed: 429"`, which is then discarded unless `-verbose` (see the swallowed-errors finding).
- `deleteBookmark` (main.go:464) likewise.
- `getSuggestedTags` (main.go:542) returns an error, recorded as a failed tag fetch.
- `getBookmarks` (main.go:393) does not check the status at all, so the 429 body fails JSON decoding and surfaces as `"failed to decode bookmarks JSON"`.

Because a 429 never slows the client down, the next request goes out on the same 3-second cadence and is rejected identically.</evidence>
<parameter name="impact">Once Pinboard starts rate-limiting — most likely when the tool is run twice in close succession, or alongside another Pinboard client — every subsequent write in the run fails and is silently dropped, while the client keeps hammering at the unchanged interval for the full duration of the account scan. The run reports a small number of successes and exits 0. Continuing to send at the same rate against a service that has explicitly asked for exponential backoff also risks the account being blocked, which the API documentation warns about for API misuse.</impact>
<parameter name="fix">Detect 429 centrally and back off. Route every Pinboard call through one helper rather than repeating `waitForRateLimit()` + `http.Get` at five sites:

```go
// pinboardGet performs a rate-limited Pinboard request, retrying with an
// exponentially widening interval on 429. Pinboard's docs require clients to
// back off on 429; a fixed-interval client keeps getting rejected for the
// whole run and silently drops every write.
func pinboardGet(apiURL string) (*http.Response, error) {
	backoff := 3 * time.Second
	for attempt := 0; attempt < 5; attempt++ {
		waitForRateLimit()
		resp, err := httpClient.Get(apiURL)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pinboard request failed: %w", err)
		}
		if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusTooManyRequests {
			return resp, nil
		}
		if closeErr := resp.Body.Close(); closeErr != nil {
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, ErrClosingBodyMsg, closeErr)
		}
		backoff *= 2
		setRateLimitInterval(backoff)
	}

	return nil, errRateLimited
}
```

with `setRateLimitInterval` calling `rateLimiter.Reset(d)` under `rateLimiterMux`. Honour a `Retry-After` header when present in preference to the doubled value.

Separately, give `posts/all` its own gate — it is called once per run, so simply documenting the 5-minute limit and not retrying it tightly is enough, but the current code would retry it at 3-second intervals.

Add a test with an `httptest` server that returns 429 twice then 200, asserting three attempts and a widened interval. Make the ticker interval a variable so the test does not take 9 seconds.</fix>
</invoke>

## Evidence

## Impact

## Fix

## Resolution
pinboardGet retries on HTTP 429 up to maxRateLimitRetries, calling widenRateLimit() which doubles rateLimitInterval and resets the ticker, as Pinboard's docs require. Exhausting the retries returns errRateLimited naming the endpoint. Error messages carry the path, never the built URL, so the auth token cannot leak into a log. Covered by TestPinboardGet_BacksOffOn429, which asserts three attempts and a widened interval. README's rate-limiting section now documents the backoff and the separate five-minute posts/all limit.
title: No 429 detection or backoff, which the Pinboard API documentation explicitly requires

## Problem

`getPageTitle` passes `resp.Body` straight to `html.Parse` with no size limit and no `Content-Type` check. Whatever a bookmarked host returns — a multi-gigabyte video, a disk image, an endless stream — is read into memory and built into a DOM.

Ten of these run concurrently by default, all under a client with no timeout.</problem>
<parameter name="evidence">main.go:473-496:

```go
func getPageTitle(urlString string) (string, error) {
	resp, err := http.Get(urlString)
	...
	if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to fetch page: status %d", resp.StatusCode)
	}

	doc, err := html.Parse(resp.Body)
```

There is no `io.LimitReader`, no `Content-Length` check, and no inspection of `resp.Header.Get("Content-Type")`. `html.Parse` reads to EOF and retains the whole tree.

The concurrency multiplier, main.go:77 and main.go:229:

```go
workers := flag.Int("workers", 10, "Number of concurrent workers for parallel processing")
...
sem := make(chan struct{}, workers)
```

and there is no client timeout to bound how long any one of them runs (filed separately).

The URLs are entirely attacker-influenced in the sense that matters here: they are arbitrary third-party hosts from the user's bookmark collection, many of them long-abandoned domains that may since have been re-registered by someone else. `getPageTitle` is reached for any bookmark with an empty title, which is precisely the set the tool goes looking for (main.go:170).

The title extraction itself is also unbounded: `extractTitleFromHTML` (main.go:501) walks the whole tree and returns `node.FirstChild.Data`, which for a crafted page is an arbitrarily long string that then becomes the bookmark title. Pinboard caps titles at 255 characters (API docs, Data Types: "`title` — up to 255 characters long"), so an over-long title is silently truncated or rejected by `posts/add`.</evidence>
<parameter name="impact">A single bookmark pointing at a large or hostile response exhausts memory for the whole process, taking the run down after it has already applied part of its changes. Ten such hosts do it ten times faster. Because bookmark collections accumulate dead domains that get re-registered, this is a realistic failure rather than a theoretical one — and the tool's own behaviour (delete on 4xx) means the operator is trusting it to make destructive decisions in the same pass.</impact>
<parameter name="fix">Bound the read and check the type before parsing:

```go
const maxTitleFetchBytes = 1 << 20 // 1 MiB is far more than any <head> needs

if ct := resp.Header.Get("Content-Type"); ct != "" {
	mediaType, _, err := mime.ParseMediaType(ct)
	if err != nil || (mediaType != "text/html" && mediaType != "application/xhtml+xml") {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("not an HTML page: %s", ct)
	}
}

// Cap the body: html.Parse reads to EOF, so an unbounded response from a
// bookmarked host would be held entirely in memory, times -workers.
doc, err := html.Parse(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, maxTitleFetchBytes))
```

`html.Parse` tolerates a truncated document, so a 1 MiB cap still yields the `<title>` for any real page.

Clamp the extracted title to Pinboard's documented 255-character limit before returning it, truncating on a rune boundary rather than a byte boundary.

Add tests for: a non-HTML `Content-Type` returning an error, a body larger than the cap still yielding the title from the head, and a title over 255 characters being truncated.</fix>
</invoke>

## Evidence

## Impact

## Fix

## Resolution
getPageTitle now rejects a non-markup Content-Type via requireHTML and parses through io.LimitReader capped at maxTitleFetchBytes (1 MiB), so an unbounded or hostile response cannot be held in memory once per worker. The extracted title is clamped to Pinboard's documented 255-character limit by truncateRunes, which cuts on rune boundaries so a multi-byte character is never split. Covered by TestRequireHTML, TestTruncateRunes, TestGetPageTitle ("rejects a non-HTML body"), and TestGetPageTitle_TruncatesToPinboardLimit.
title: getPageTitle parses an unbounded, content-type-unchecked remote body as HTML across ten workers

## Problem

`getBookmarks` is the only Pinboard call that does not check `resp.StatusCode`. It hands the body straight to `json.Decoder` regardless. Pinboard answers an unauthenticated request with HTTP 401 and the plain-text body `API requires authentication`, and a throttled one with HTTP 429 — neither of which is JSON, so the decode fails and the caller receives an error that names the wrong problem.

Nothing downstream can recover the real cause: the status code is discarded before the error is built.</problem>
<parameter name="evidence">main.go:379-397 — no status check between the request and the decode:

```go
func getBookmarks(apiToken string) ([]Bookmark, error) {
	waitForRateLimit()
	resp, err := http.Get(fmt.Sprintf("%s/posts/all?auth_token=%s&format=json", ...))
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to fetch bookmarks from Pinboard API: %w", err)
	}
	defer func() { ... }()
	var bookmarks []Bookmark
	if err := json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode(&bookmarks); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to decode bookmarks JSON: %w", err)
	}
```

Compare the other four calls, which all check it — main.go:439, main.go:464, main.go:487, main.go:542. `getBookmarks` is the outlier.

The real 401 response, confirmed against the live endpoint:

```
$ curl -s -o body -w 'status=%{http_code} ctype=%{content_type}\n' \
    'https://api.pinboard.in/v1/posts/suggest?url=http%3A%2F%2Fexample.com&auth_token=nobody%3ANOTAREALTOKEN'
status=401 ctype=text/html; charset=UTF-8
$ cat body
API requires authentication
```

So a revoked token produces:

```
Error fetching bookmarks: failed to decode bookmarks JSON: invalid character 'A' looking for beginning of value
```

`TestGetBookmarks_InvalidToken` (main_functions_test.go:401) asserts only `err == nil` is false, so it passes on the misleading message and does not pin the cause.

Pinboard API documentation, Rate Limits:

> Make sure your API clients check for `429 Too Many Requests` server errors and back off appropriately.

`posts/all` is additionally limited to once every five minutes, so 429 here is the expected response to a re-run within that window — the single most likely failure this function will see.</evidence>
<parameter name="impact">The most common operational failures — an expired or revoked token, and a re-run inside the 5-minute `posts/all` window — are both reported as malformed JSON. The operator is pointed at a parsing problem in the tool rather than at their credentials or at rate limiting, and because the fetch failure also exits 0 (filed separately), a scheduled run reports success while producing this message. The status code needed to tell the two apart is available and thrown away.</impact>
<parameter name="fix">Check the status before decoding, and name the two cases the caller can act on:

```go
switch resp.StatusCode {
case http.StatusOK:
case http.StatusUnauthorized:
	return nil, fmt.Errorf("pinboard rejected the API token (HTTP 401); check %s", tokenName)
case http.StatusTooManyRequests:
	// posts/all is limited to one call every five minutes.
	return nil, fmt.Errorf("pinboard rate limit hit (HTTP 429); posts/all allows one call per five minutes")
default:
	return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to fetch bookmarks: status %d", resp.StatusCode)
}
```

Once the shared `pinboardGet` helper from the 429-backoff finding exists, this check belongs there and `getBookmarks` inherits it — do not duplicate the switch at five call sites.

Tighten `TestGetBookmarks_InvalidToken` to assert the returned error mentions the token rather than merely being non-nil, and add a 429 case. The existing test already serves a 401 with a non-JSON body, so it needs only the assertion.</fix>
</invoke>

## Evidence

## Impact

## Fix

## Resolution
Added checkPinboardStatus, called by getBookmarks and every other Pinboard call before decoding. A 401 now returns an error naming PINBOARD_API_TOKEN instead of surfacing as "failed to decode bookmarks JSON"; 429 is absorbed by the backoff in pinboardGet. Covered by TestGetBookmarks_InvalidTokenNamesTheToken, which asserts the error text names the env var rather than only that it is non-nil.
title: getBookmarks never checks the HTTP status, so auth and rate-limit failures surface as a JSON decode error

## Problem

The repository carries a detailed `.golangci.yml` — 30+ enabled linters, per-linter settings, exclusion rules, `issues-exit-code: 1` — and no workflow ever invokes it. CI runs only `go build` and `go test`. The lint configuration is therefore advisory-only: it constrains whoever happens to run the tool locally and gates nothing.

The test step also omits `-race`, on a program whose central design is a worker pool sharing a mutable global `Statistics`.</problem>
<parameter name="evidence">.github/workflows/go.yml:24-28 — the complete set of checks:

```yaml
    - name: Build
      run: go build -v ./...

    - name: Test
      run: go test -v ./...
```

No `golangci-lint` step, no `go vet`, no `-race`, no `-coverprofile`.

.golangci.yml:1-10 declares an exit code that nothing consumes:

```yaml
version: "2"

run:
  timeout: 5m
  issues-exit-code: 1
```

and enables the linters at .golangci.yml:30-80, including `gosec`, `bodyclose`, `errcheck`, `wrapcheck`, `paralleltest`, and `unparam`.

Running it now reports 13 unaddressed issues:

```
$ golangci-lint run --timeout 5m
apply_functions_test.go:13:27: string `http://example.com` has 28 occurrences, make it a constant (goconst)
...
13 issues:
* goconst: 13
```

.golangci.yml:190 also sets `fix: true`, so anyone invoking `golangci-lint run` locally has their working tree rewritten as a side effect — a surprising default for a command usually treated as read-only, and one reason a CI step would need `--fix=false`.

Separately, `run.go` is pinned to `"1.25"` (.golangci.yml:12) while the workflow installs Go 1.26 (.github/workflows/go.yml:22) and `go.mod` declares `go 1.25.6` — three different answers to what version this project targets.</evidence>
<parameter name="impact">Every linter the project configured for itself — including `gosec` for security and `bodyclose` for leaked response bodies — is unenforced on pull requests. Thirteen issues are already outstanding with nothing to surface them. The absence of `-race` means a data race introduced into the worker pool would merge green; the suite does pass under `-race` today, so this is a gate worth having rather than a known failure being hidden.</impact>
<parameter name="fix">Add a lint job to `.github/workflows/go.yml`:

```yaml
  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
    - uses: actions/setup-go@b7ad1dad31e06c5925ef5d2fc7ad053ef454303e # v7
      with:
        go-version-file: go.mod
    - uses: golangci/golangci-lint-action@<pinned-digest> # v9
      with:
        version: v2.5.0
        args: --timeout 5m --fix=false
```

`--fix=false` is required because the config sets `fix: true`; without it CI would rewrite files and lint whatever it just produced.

Change the test step to gate on races and record coverage:

```yaml
    - name: Test
      run: go test -race -coverprofile=coverage.out ./...
```

Use `go-version-file: go.mod` in both jobs instead of the hardcoded `'1.26'`, so the toolchain follows the module and the three version declarations converge. Then set `run.go` in `.golangci.yml` to match, or remove it and let golangci-lint read `go.mod`.

Clear the 13 outstanding `goconst` issues (all in test files) before turning the gate on, or add a scoped exclusion for `goconst` in `_test.go` files if shared URL fixtures are not wanted.</fix>
</invoke>

## Evidence

## Impact

## Fix

## Resolution
Added a lint job to .github/workflows/go.yml using golangci/golangci-lint-action pinned to commit ba0d7d2ec06a0ea1cb5fa41b2e4a3ab91d21278a (v9.3.0), running golangci-lint v2.12.2 with --fix=false to override the config's issues.fix: true. Test step now runs -race with -coverprofile. Both jobs use go-version-file: go.mod instead of a hardcoded version; .golangci.yml's separate run.go pin was removed and its stale version comment corrected, so go.mod is the single source of truth. All 13 outstanding goconst issues were cleared first (shared test constants), so the gate starts green: golangci-lint reports 0 issues.
title: CI never runs golangci-lint despite a 216-line config, and runs tests without -race or a coverage gate

## Problem

`.github/workflows/go.yml` has no `permissions:` key at either workflow or job level. GitHub then applies the repository or organisation default, which for repositories created before the default changed — or where the setting was never tightened — is read *and write* across contents, issues, pull requests, packages, and more.

The build and test job needs `contents: read` and nothing else. The release workflow does set permissions, so the omission here is an inconsistency within the same repository rather than a house style.</problem>
<parameter name="evidence">.github/workflows/go.yml:1-16 — no `permissions` anywhere:

```yaml
name: Go test build

on:
  push:
    branches: [ "main" ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ "main" ]

jobs:

  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
```

.github/workflows/release.yml:4-6 — the sibling workflow does declare them:

```yaml
permissions:
    contents: write
    packages: write
```

The job runs `go build ./...` and `go test ./...` (lines 24-28). `go test` executes arbitrary test code, and this suite in particular makes outbound network calls to tinyurl.com, is.gd, and api.pinboard.in (filed separately) — so the token is exposed to a job that both talks to the internet and compiles third-party module code.

On the positive side, both action references are correctly pinned to full commit SHAs with version comments, and neither workflow interpolates untrusted input into a `run:` block, so there is no script-injection surface here.

The release workflow's `packages: write` is also unused — `wangyoucao577/go-release-action` uploads release assets, which `contents: write` covers; nothing publishes a package.</evidence>
<parameter name="impact">A compromised dependency or action in the build job — or a malicious test in a pull request from a fork, for the `pull_request` trigger — receives a `GITHUB_TOKEN` scoped far beyond what the job needs, potentially able to push commits, alter issues, or publish packages. Least privilege here costs two lines and removes the entire class.</impact>
<parameter name="fix">Add an explicit least-privilege block to `.github/workflows/go.yml`:

```yaml
permissions:
  contents: read
```

at the workflow level, immediately after the `on:` block. Any job needing more (none currently) can widen it locally.

Trim the release workflow to what it actually uses:

```yaml
permissions:
    contents: write
```

Dropping `packages: write` — no step publishes a package.

Set the organisation or repository default workflow permissions to read-only under Settings → Actions → General, so a future workflow that forgets the block fails closed rather than open.</fix>
</invoke>

## Evidence

## Impact

## Fix

## Resolution
Added `permissions: contents: read` at workflow level in .github/workflows/go.yml, covering both the build and the new lint job. Removed the unused `packages: write` from .github/workflows/release.yml, leaving `contents: write` for the release assets it actually uploads. Setting the repository default workflow permission to read-only remains a GitHub settings change outside the repo and is not covered here.
title: The build workflow declares no permissions block, so GITHUB_TOKEN gets the repository default scope

## Problem

`README.md` refers the reader to a LICENSE file for the project's terms. No such file exists anywhere in the repository, and `go.mod` declares no license either. A public repository with no license grant is "all rights reserved" by default — nobody may legally copy, modify, or redistribute it, which contradicts the README's own invitation to fork and contribute.

The release workflow was evidently meant to ship the file: the line that would attach it is commented out.</problem>

See LICENSE file for details.

$ git ls-files
